messages:
Alex: Kicking off a multi-region "cascade" stormbench to validate routing priming + KV behavior across failovers. Goal: apples-to-apples compare of (a) synth arrival shapes vs replay harness, (b) kernel selection toggles, and (c) warm vs cold KV priming. Link to run plan: https://internal/runs/1971234567 🚀

Priya: Nice. Quick Q — are we including a dedicated warm-priming pass before the main run? cold priming can mask batching gains.

Alex: Yes — plan is: 1) priming pass (prefixes from sampled replays), 2) synth spike with same arrival shape, 3) replay run with throttling to match synth QPS. Keep model/quant fixed (llama-13b-fp16-qat) so kernels are comparable.

Rui: We should also freeze kernel-picker config for the comparison. Kernel heuristics changed in 1769 and caused noisy p95s last month. For the run: set KERNEL_PICKER=stable_2025-01.

Sam: Left a tiny spreadsheet in the plan with metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec per-GPU, batch-size distribution, kernel chosen fraction, kv-hit-rate by prefix age, and cost-per-1k-tokens.

Maya: FYI I saw a perf regression on a canary after the kernel heuristics tweak — p95 up ~12% for short seqs. Can we include a short-only workload (seq_len <=64) as a control?

Alex: Good call — adding 'short' and 'long' lanes. Also adding a 'drain' scenario: region-B drains while traffic routed to region-A fallback models (primary->secondary, weighted-split, and conservative-fallback).

Jordan: For KV priming, use the replay prefix extractor script I made last quarter. It preserves prefix distribution and realistic token counts. Command is:
```
./tools/extract_prefixes.py --replay /mnt/replays/2025-01/replay.tar.gz --out primeset.json --sample 100k
./tools/prime_kv.sh --primes primeset.json --region us-east-1 --parallel 32
```
Should be ~20m to prime 100k prefixes on a 6-node pool.

Priya: Also add a 'no-prime' baseline instead of only cold vs warm. Cold sometimes still shows warmish behavior due to implicit caching. Want to quantify that.

Rui: About apples-to-apples: ensure the same runtime binary + kernel libs on both regions. Last time we had a mismatch in cuBlas/cuDNN versions and it skewed kernel selection.

Sam: Saw an interesting artifact: when arrival shape is identical but KV is warm, batching compresses more effectively (median batch size +18%) which reduces p50 by ~25% in synth runs. I'll capture batch-size CDFs.

Alex: Good. For routing failover patterns: schedule three cases: immediate failover (all traffic switch), progressive ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100% over 60s), and probabilistic fallback (10% of requests route to fallback when primary overloaded). We'll capture added network RTT + routing decision latency.

Maya: Can we instrument kernel selection traces? Tiny header per-request that records kernel id and batch size. We already have that on canary, right?

Jordan: Yes — add --trace-kernel to the harness. Trace format is a single-line CSV: ts,req_id,kernel_id,batch_size,seq_len,kv_hit. We can ingest those into the perf pipeline.

Sam: Sharing quick baseline numbers from a short local run (warm-prime vs no-prime, synth spike):
- warm-prime p50: 42ms, p95: 125ms, tokens/s/GPU: 360
- no-prime p50: 58ms, p95: 210ms, tokens/s/GPU: 220
- batch-size median warm: 12, no-prime: 6
These are with KERNEL_PICKER=stable_2025-01.

Priya: Who's owning the multi-region job orchestration? Need to ensure zones have same instance types + kernel libs.

Alex: Jordan will coordinate infra. Jordan — can you queue the run tomorrow 10:00 UTC and tag eng-runtime?

Jordan: Yep. Queued run 'cascade-stormbench' for 1971234567. Regions: us-east-1 / eu-west-1 / ap-southeast-1. Using the pinned runtime image (rti-2025-01-03).

loadtest-bot: Run queued: cascade-stormbench (id=1971234567) started at 1971234575. Artifacts will be in https://internal/artifacts/1971234567 once complete.

Alex: After run completes, we'll do an apples-to-apples diff: same runtime, same model bits, same arrival shape, and compare kernel selection entropy and kv-hit tail behavior. If we see the kernel regression again, revert kernel-picker and re-run the short lane.

Maya: If we find a regression tied to kernel heuristics, I propose a mitigations matrix: a) revert picker, b) restrict picker where seq_len<128, c) force kernel per-model until we understand perf space.

Sam: Also proposing a synthetic microbenchmark (single-request sequences with controlled batch sizes) to isolate kernel perfs outside of batching noise. Small script to feed 1k requests at controlled inter-arrival times.

Alex: Perfect. Plan looks solid. We'll reconvene after artifacts are up and we have initial p95 diffs. Thanks all :thumbsup:

loadtest-bot: Run completed at 1971234590. Artifacts uploaded: https://internal/artifacts/1971234567/logs.tar.gz , https://internal/artifacts/1971234567/traces.csv , https://internal/artifacts/1971234567/metrics.json

Priya: Downloading traces now. Will start basic kernel-entropy + kv-hit tail analysis and post highlights in this thread.

Jordan: Leaving a note: if anybody wants to spin variants (different kernel picks, or no-KV optimistic cache), reply here and I'll requeue small runs.

Alex: Great. We'll aim for a short follow-up sync tomorrow after initial analysis.
